title: Frontend routing mismatch during canary swap caused rollback cascade and scale-back surge
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a planned canary swap for model v2026-03-b, an inconsistency between the frontend routing proxy and the rollout controller caused a percentage of traffic to be misattributed to the old variant while the rollout controller believed the canary was active. Concurrent autoscaler activity (scale-down based on a transient CPU observation) removed capacity from the old variant during the partial traffic split, which triggered multiple automated rollbacks and then a cascading scale-back surge across both variants. The result was elevated latency for ~18 minutes and ~8% request error increase for a subset of enterprise customers in us-west-2.

Impact:
- Duration: 00:18:00 (2026-03-10T14:12:00Z -> 2026-03-10T14:30:00Z)
- Affected customers: ~12 orgs (enterprise tier) with requests routed through the affected edge pool
- Error types: 5xx spikes (gateway 502/504), timeouts from downstream model runtime, and increased tail latency (+320ms p99)
- Business impact: transient SLA violations for affected customers, several support tickets from customers noticing degraded response quality.

What happened (high-level):
1) Canary swap initiated by release-engineering to promote v2026-03-b from 5% to 40% traffic using the rollout controller.
2) Frontend proxy configuration (edge-router) received the new routing weights one minute before the rollout controller finished applying its internal route epoch, creating a short window where the edge and control-plane disagreed on which backend should handle specific headers.
3) The disagreement caused sticky-route header normalization to route some traffic to the older variant while the control-plane attempted to transition the target.
4) Autoscaler observed a transient CPU dip on the old variant (false negative from a noisy monitoring sample) and scaled the old variant down by 30% during the disagreement window.
5) The old variant with reduced capacity dropped requests causing the control-plane health signal to trigger an automated rollback attempt. The rollback flow attempted to re-pin routes and scale the old variant back up, but the pinned version state and the edge's stale route cache conflicted, producing a rollback loop and extra control-plane churn.
6) To protect global SLOs, auto-fallback policies engaged, which re-routed remaining traffic to a warm fallback cluster causing a temporary capacity surge there and increased cross-cluster latency.

Root causes (confirmed and contributing):
- Race condition between edge-router config propagation and rollout controller epoch application. Edge applied weights earlier than the control-plane completed pin operations.
- Sticky-route header normalization logic in the edge did not include a rollout-epoch tag, so route affinity could be satisfied against stale assignments.
- Autoscaler sampling window too aggressive for short-lived load shifts; single transient sample triggered scale-down without quorum.
- Rollback flow expected optimistic re-pinning to be idempotent; stale route caches in proxies made re-pinning non-deterministic.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Manually pinned the rollout to the previous stable variant (rollback stop) while engineers paused automated rollbacks. (Ops action by @Miguel Alvarez, 14:20Z)
- Increased concurrent capacity on fallback pool by +40% to absorb surge and reduce errors (infra action 14:22Z).
- Flushed edge-router route cache across the affected edge nodes to remove stale assignments (infra+edge team, 14:25Z).
- Temporarily disabled the aggressive autoscaler window for the old variant to avoid further scale-downs during investigation (14:28Z).

Why the existing safeguards didn’t prevent this:
- Rollout controller and edge-router use separate propagation channels; there is no strict two-phase commit or epoch-guard between them.
- Rollout affinity assumptions rely on consistent epoch metadata being available to the edge, which is not yet propagated atomically.
- Autoscaler decision rules are tuned for steady-state elasticity, not high-churn rollout windows.

Action items (owners and target dates):
- Add rollout-epoch propagation to edge-router config and require epoch match for sticky-route binding. Owner: @Leila Chen. Due: 2026-03-24.
- Add a short (30s) rollout stabilization hold that prevents autoscaler scale-downs for instances that are part of active rollouts. Owner: @Miguel Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Implement a two-phase rollout apply in the controller: stage weights -> confirm edge epoch -> commit pin. Owner: @Samir Rao. Due: 2026-04-04.
- Harden rollback path to be idempotent with explicit cache-invalidation handshake: when re-pinning, send a cache-flush request to all proxies before changing weights. Owner: @Aisha Patel. Due: 2026-03-31.
- Improve autoscaler sampling to require two consecutive low samples (quorum) before scaling down during rollout windows. Owner: @Infra-Autoscale. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Create a telemetry dashboard showing rollout epoch drift and edge vs control-plane weight divergence with alerting at 2% divergence. Owner: @Observability. Due: 2026-03-16.

Follow-up testing and verification plan:
- Run synthetic canary promotions in the staging environment with induced delays in config propagation to validate two-phase commit behavior (QA + Release Eng). Test window: 2026-03-15 -> 2026-03-18.
- Add chaos test that forces a transient autoscaler false-negative and observe system behavior (SRE + Autoscale). Target: 2026-03-21.
- Post-deploy verification: run three real canary promotions for low-traffic internal models and validate no edge-control divergence across all regions. Target: 2026-04-05.

Communications and tickets created:
- Customer support escalation ticket list created and triaged. Support lead: @Nina Ortiz. Ticket IDs: SUP-9812..SUP-9823.
- Incident timeline and raw logs uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/rollout-ENG-263901 (internal).
- Related GitHub PR to add epoch tag to edge config: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-router/pull/8341

Notes and decisions to surface for leadership:
- Short-term fixes (disable autoscale down and flush caches) should be automated next release to reduce human-in-the-loop time.
- Two-phase commit model across control-plane and edge has moderate engineering cost but materially reduces risk for high-traffic rollouts; recommend prioritization in runtime-1.20 roadmap.

Expected follow-up milestones after owners complete action items:
- 2026-03-16: Dashboard + alerting live.
- 2026-03-20: Autoscaler sampling change deployed to canary cluster.
- 2026-03-24: Edge epoch propagation merged and rolling deploy to us-west region.
- 2026-04-04: Two-phase commit model merged to rollout controller and staged in staging, with rollout experiments next week.

2026-03-10 14:20Z - Ops: manual pin applied to stop automated rollback loop; action owner: Miguel Alvarez.
